title: Separable Choice
transcript:
• Joint probabilistic choice rule ρ(y1 , y2 ; x1 , x2 ): Frodo faces x1 and chooses y1 ;
   Sam faces x2 and chooses y2 .
 • Separable choice: c1 , c2 assign feasible actions to every own choice problem. Their
   joint distribution is µ:

                                   c1 ,c2

 • One µ for all choice problems, allowing arbitrarily correlated plans.
 • What? Characterization of Separable Choice [Chambers et al., 2024].
 • Why? Detection of corruption: match-rigging, rotten apples, collusion, agentic
   coordination; peer effects [Sacerdote, 2011]; influence; dynamic choice
   [Frick et al., 2019].
 • How? No signalling. No Entanglement.

title: Separable Restrictions on Separable Choice
transcript:
• For a valid normalized joint rule ρ, the following are equivalent:

Lemma
 1. ρ is separable.
 2. There exists µ ≥ 0 with 1> µ = 1 and ρ = Aµ.
 3. There exists µ ≥ 0 with ρ = Aµ.


 • The normalization in (2) is implied by (3) when ρ is valid and normalized.
htmlTranscript:
• For a valid normalized joint rule ρ\rho, the following are equivalent:

  1. ρ\rho is separable.

  2. There exists μ≥0\mu\geq0 with 𝟏⊤μ=1\mathbf{1}^{\top}\mu=1 and ρ=Aμ\rho=A\mu.

  3. There exists μ≥0\mu\geq0 with ρ=Aμ\rho=A\mu.

  • The normalization in (2) is implied by (3) when ρ\rho is valid and normalized.

title: Afriat-Style Characterization of Separability
transcript:
Theorem
The following are equivalent:

 1. ρ is separable.
 2. For every finite k ≥ 1, there exists an extension q satisfying no signalling with qj = ρ
    for every Sam copy j.
 3. At k = |X2 |, there exists an extension q satisfying no signalling with q̄ = ρ pointwise.


 • Like Afriat’s test, ours checks linear feasibility [Afriat, 1967].

The following are equivalent:

title: Why One Copy per Sam Covariate Suffices
transcript:
1. Equalize the copies. Average the extension over relabelings of Sam’s copies. Every
    Frodo–Sam marginal now equals the original average ρ.
 2. Read off a complete Sam plan. Assign a different Sam covariate to each copy.
    The vector of their actions is a plan c2 . No signalling makes its distribution the same
    at every Frodo covariate.
 3. Build Frodo’s plan. Given c2 with positive mass, use the extension’s conditional
    choice probabilities to draw a Frodo action at each x1 . Taking their product gives a
    distribution over complete Frodo plans c1 . Mixing over c2 recovers each observed pair
    marginal ρ.

Conversely, a separable mixture gives any number of copies by letting them all use the
same Sam plan.
htmlTranscript:
1. Equalize the copies. Average the extension over relabelings of Sam’s copies. Every Frodo–Sam marginal now equals the original average ρ\rho.

  2. Read off a complete Sam plan. Assign a different Sam covariate to each copy. The vector of their actions is a plan c2c_2. No signalling makes its distribution the same at every Frodo covariate.

  3. Build Frodo’s plan. Given c2c_2 with positive mass, use the extension’s conditional choice probabilities to draw a Frodo action at each x1x_1. Taking their product gives a distribution over complete Frodo plans c1c_1. Mixing over c2c_2 recovers each observed pair marginal ρ\rho.

Conversely, a separable mixture gives any number of copies by letting them all use the same Sam plan.

title: Relation with the Literature
transcript:
• Marginality and nonnegative joint Block–Marschak sums can hold even when joint
   choice fails separable random utility [Chambers et al., 2024].
 • Our test for finite covariate domains asks whether the observed rule admits a no
   signalling replica extension.
 • The online appendix by Aguiar and Kashaev derives the resulting linear inequalities in
   observed probabilities.

  • The online appendix by Aguiar and Kashaev derives the resulting linear inequalities in observed probabilities.

title: Why Test Agentic Separability?
transcript:
• Shared hardware. In a controlled test, OpenAI agents in separate virtual machines
   exchanged synthetic secrets by timing reads from the same processor cache. [OpenAI,

   compromised Hugging Face systems. [OpenAI, August 2026] [Hugging Face, July 2026]

title: The Agentic Stress Test
transcript:
We build a controlled test in which Qwen infers hidden charges and a programmed rule
uses those beliefs to choose pleas.

 • Frodo and Sam each see their own charge, small or large. Both see the judge and a
   public signal that assigns roles.
 • With at least one small charge, the judge rewards matching pleas that suit the judge
   type. With two large charges, the judge rewards opposite pleas.

Can marginal plea frequencies stay stable while coordination exceeds the separable bound?

title: Conclusions
transcript:
• Separable choice is one mixture over feasible local plans, with arbitrary correlation
  across plans.
• In the binary domain, no signalling plus CHSH exactly characterizes separability; no
  signalling alone can miss nonseparable rules.
• With finitely many covariates and actions, separability holds exactly when there is a
  joint rule for Frodo and one Sam copy per Sam covariate that satisfies no signalling
  and reproduces the observed rule on average. The appendix shows when the tensor
  product of the individual inequalities characterizes joint choice.
• In the agentic check, CHSH rejects separability in all 20 runs, while the no signalling
  test never rejects.
htmlTranscript:
• Separable choice is one mixture over feasible local plans, with arbitrary correlation across plans.

  • In the binary domain, no signalling plus CHSH exactly characterizes separability; no signalling alone can miss nonseparable rules.

  • With finitely many covariates and actions, separability holds exactly when there is a joint rule for Frodo and one Sam copy per Sam covariate that satisfies no signalling and reproduces the observed rule on average. The appendix shows when the tensor product of the individual inequalities characterizes joint choice.

  • In the agentic check, CHSH rejects separability in all 20 runs, while the no signalling test never rejects.

title: Soccer: How We Build the Sample
transcript:
• Start with 92 final-round group matches from 12 UEFA European Championships
     (1980–2024), using the international results archive.
   • Reconstruct each group’s points table before kickoff. Pair each fixture with the
     simultaneous match between the other two teams in that group.
   • For each team, cross a win or draw in its own match with each of the three possible
     results of the other match. Count direct qualification only if it survives the least
     favorable resolution of a points tie.
   • Keep a fixture if both teams can be assigned a state from these pre-match scenarios.
     This leaves 53 matches. Use their full-time results only after the states are fixed.
htmlTranscript:
• Start with 9292 final-round group matches from 1212 UEFA European Championships (1980–2024), using the international results archive.

  • Reconstruct each group’s points table before kickoff. Pair each fixture with the simultaneous match between the other two teams in that group.

  • For each team, cross a win or draw in its own match with each of the three possible results of the other match. Count direct qualification only if it survives the least favorable resolution of a points tie.

  • Keep a fixture if both teams can be assigned a state from these pre-match scenarios. This leaves 5353 matches. Use their full-time results only after the states are fixed.
